_comment: Instruction-selection contract for the gfx950 code objects, asserted by asm_audit.py
against the disassembly. These exist because the register-cliff check in build_gfx950.sh
catches only kernels that will not LAUNCH. The failure that actually costs throughput is a
kernel that launches, is numerically correct, and quietly runs on the wrong instruction --
the K16 fp8 MFMA instead of the wide-K one (measured 1x vs 2x bf16 on this GPU), or an fp4
operand widened to bf16 because a convert did not fold. With no AMD GPU on the dev box that
is invisible until benchmark day, which is exactly the day there is no time to fix it.
Keys are object-name substrings; the LONGEST match wins, so interp_decode_fp8 does not also
inherit interp_decode's rules. Values are kernel-name substrings -> checks.
_arch is asserted against each object's own ELF header before any rule runs. It is not a
label: the fp8 contract here is the INVERSE of scripts/asm_expect_gfx942.json's, because the
instruction this file forbids is the only fp8 MFMA CDNA3 has.
_a4w4_note: The A4W4 grouped MoE prefill GEMM must run MXFP4 on BOTH operands through the matrix core.
Two silent failures are waiting and ONLY the disassembly sees either:
(a) the fp4 operand widened back to bf16 because a convert did not fold -- that is w4a16
wearing an A4W4 name, correct numerically and half the throughput;
(b) the backend selecting the UNSCALED v_mfma_f32_32x32x64_f8f6f4, which it does whenever
the E8M0 scale arguments are compile-time constants, silently discarding microscaling.
Both are measured facts -- see runtime/tests/a4w4_gfx950_test.hip.
SCOPING, which took three tries and is worth stating so it is not 'simplified' back:
* not plow_exec -- the compiler OUTLINES the two grouped wrappers, so plow_exec holds none
* the two wrapper names are spelled out rather than matched by the common d_moe_group
prefix, because that prefix also catches d_moe_group_pf_t (the bf16/block-fp8 body), which
the _gq object outlines separately and which correctly contains no scaled MFMA;
* the format check is fmt_on and NOT the kernel-wide cbsz/blgp rules, because i[3] selects
the encoding at RUNTIME so each wrapper also holds the bf16 body's MFMAs -- and a bf16
MFMA carries no cbsz field, which reads as 0 and would trip a kernel-wide 'cbsz: 4'.
4 scaled MFMAs per wrapper = SM*SN=2 accumulators x 2 K=64 MFMAs per staged BK=128 tile.
_moe_pf_note: The grouped-expert prefill GEMM must stay ON THE MATRIX CORE. If this arm ever loses its
MFMA it has silently degraded to a per-output VALU dot, and sorting the tokens by expert --
the entire point of the op -- buys nothing.
_fp8kv_flash_note: interp_flash_fp8kv is the 4-wave class-4 object for an fp8-KV packet, and its FA_DBUF=1 PREFETCH path had no FP8KV branch at all: it read the e4m3 cache with ld_glob8 (16 bytes per 8 elements) instead of 8, ran off the end of every row, and never applied the row scale. d_flash_prefill<D,true> COMPILED fine under FA_DBUF=1 -- the wrong dtype was silent, and the only symptom was a GPU memory fault the first time segmented dispatch actually sent class-4 segments to this object. The assertion below is the shape of the fix, not its spelling: the fp8 path MUST show the e4m3 unpack converts, and the bf16 twin must show none.
